exploit_linux/ssh/openssh_musl_crypt_byp.name: OpenSSH musl-libc crypt() Authentication Bypass
author: Özgün Kültekin
Emanuele Cervelli
exploit_linux/ssh/openssh_musl_crypt_byp.description:
On musl-libc based systems (Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, Buildroot, etc.),
          OpenSSH password authentication can be bypassed for accounts whose
          /etc/shadow password field is "*" (locked).

          musl's crypt() implementation returns "*" when given a password longer
          than 256 bytes. sshd compares this return value directly against the
          shadow field, which is also "*", so authentication succeeds.

          The exploit requires two password attempts on the same SSH connection:
          the first (any short password) primes sshd's internal fake-salt cache
          with a real $5$/$6$ hash from another account on the system, and the
          second (>256 byte) password triggers the musl crypt() bypass.

          All five conditions must be true:
          1. OpenSSH built against musl (not glibc)
          2. sshd built without PAM, or UsePAM no (Alpine default)
          3. PasswordAuthentication yes (OpenSSH default)
          4. Target account has "*" in /etc/shadow password field
          5. At least one other account has a real $5$ or $6$ hash

          musl has returned "*" on overlength passwords since 2012. sshd started
          borrowing other accounts' salts in 2016. The bug is exploitable on
          OpenSSH as far back as 7.5p1 (musl 1.1.16, 2017).

          Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 (2026-11-05).

exploit_unix/ftp/vsftpd_234_backdoor.name: VSFTPD 2.3.4 Backdoor Command Execution
author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
MC <mc@metasploit.com>
g0tmi1k
exploit_unix/ftp/vsftpd_234_backdoor.description:
This module exploits a malicious backdoor that was added to the VSFTPD download
          archive. This backdoor was introduced into the vsftpd-2.3.4.tar.gz archive between
          June 30th 2011 and July 1st 2011 according to the most recent information
          available. This backdoor was removed on July 3rd 2011.

auxiliary_admin/2wire/xslt_password_rese.name: 2Wire Cross-Site Request Forgery Password Reset Vulnerability
author: hkm <hkm@hakim.ws>
Travis Phillips
auxiliary_admin/2wire/xslt_password_rese.description:
This module will reset the admin password on a 2Wire wireless router.  This is
          done by using the /xslt page where authentication is not required, thus allowing
          configuration changes (such as resetting the password) as administrators.

auxiliary_admin/android/google_play_stor.name: Android Browser RCE Through Google Play Store XFO
author: Rafay Baloch
joev <joev@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_admin/android/google_play_stor.description:
This module combines two vulnerabilities to achieve remote code
          execution on affected Android devices. First, the module exploits
          CVE-2014-6041, a Universal Cross-Site Scripting (UXSS) vulnerability present in
          versions of Android's open source stock browser (the AOSP Browser) prior to
          4.4. Second, the Google Play store's web interface fails to enforce a
          X-Frame-Options: DENY header (XFO) on some error pages, and therefore, can be
          targeted for script injection. As a result, this leads to remote code execution
          through Google Play's remote installation feature, as any application available
          on the Google Play store can be installed and launched on the user's device.

          This module requires that the user is logged into Google with a vulnerable browser.

          To list the activities in an APK, you can use `aapt dump badging /path/to/app.apk`.
